question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the edge of the road (to the right),b:Turn them away from the edge of the road (to the left),c:Keep them straight
note: When parking uphill without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic and off the roadway instead of into the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it required to signal when changing lanes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must signal whenever you change lanes so other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions and can adjust safely. Signaling is required even if you think no one is around.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does ''yield'' also require you to stop if you cannot merge safely into traffic?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop. If you cannot safely merge into traffic, you must stop and wait until there is a safe gap before proceeding.

question: The statement 'Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane and should be passed like other vehicles' is:
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to use a full traffic lane just like any other vehicle. When passing a motorcycle, move fully into the adjacent lane and give them the same space and clearance you would give a car.

question: You are being tailgated. What should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Maintain the same distance as usual,b:Increase the space ahead of your vehicle,c:Decrease your following distance
note: If you are being tailgated, increase your following distance from the vehicle ahead. This gives you more time to slow down gradually and reduces the chance of a rear-end collision if you must brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction, you should:
options: a:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing,c:Pass as slowly as possible
note: When you pass, you should move into the passing lane, accelerate to safely and efficiently overtake the other vehicle, and then return to your lane as soon as it is safe. Do not linger in the blind spot or beside the other vehicle. Return only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers,b:Drink coffee and continue,c:Open a window and keep driving
note: The safest option when tired is to stop and rest or have another licensed driver take over.

question: When weather or low visibility requires lights, which should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:High beam headlights,c:Parking lights
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not sufficient for visibility or to meet legal requirements when visibility is reduced.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts,c:Use only the lap belt
note: A combination lap and shoulder belt is designed to be worn together: the lap belt low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt across the chest and away from the neck. Using only one part greatly reduces protection and increases the risk of serious injury in a crash.

question: At a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed,b:Slow down, look and listen for trains,c:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly
note: At a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, you must approach with caution: slow down, look carefully in both directions, and listen for trains. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks without stopping.

question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change as a vehicle's speed increases?
options: a:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.,b:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,c:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: As speed increases, both stopping distance and crash severity increase. Your vehicle needs more distance to come to a complete stop, and the force of impact in a collision is much greater at higher speeds. This is why you should leave more following distance as your speed rises.

question: A vehicle with a bad suspension can cause which problem?
options: a:Squealing brakes,b:Vehicle control problems,c:Slack in the steering
note: A bad or worn suspension makes it harder to keep the vehicle stable and under control, especially when turning, braking, or driving over bumps. This can cause swaying, bouncing, and poor handling, which are serious vehicle control problems and a safety hazard.

question: For quick and controlled turns, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: For quick, controlled turns, place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel, typically around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions. This gives you better leverage, balance, and control of the vehicle, especially at higher speeds or during sudden maneuvers.

question: When your traffic signal turns green while waiting at an intersection, should you still look before proceeding?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When the light turns green, you must still look left, right, and ahead before moving. A green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but other drivers may run the red light or pedestrians may still be crossing. Checking first helps prevent collisions.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads, what should you do?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Slow down.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: On wet roads, slow down to reduce the risk of losing traction or hydroplaning. Lower speed allows your tires to maintain better contact with the road. Avoid sudden steering, hard braking, or quick acceleration, as these can cause skids when the road is slippery.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and not allowed for traffic on the side with the solid line. This marking separates traffic moving in opposite directions and controls where it is safe and legal to pass.

question: If you are on a highway next to a single broken white line, are you allowed to cross it?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass,b:You may cross to pass or change lanes,c:You may only cross it from the left lane
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors, blind spots, and signaling.

question: What is the penalty for illegally passing a stopped school bus in Illinois?
options: a:Driving privilege suspension and a mandatory $300 fine,b:A 60-day suspension of driving privileges,c:A $30 fine and 14-day suspension
note: In Illinois, illegally passing a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended carries a mandatory minimum $300 fine and a suspension of driving privileges for the first offense. The law is strict to protect children who may be crossing the road around the bus.

question: If you are involved in or come upon a traffic crash, should you stop in a safe, well-lit public place that does not obstruct traffic if able?
options: a:True,b:False
note: If you are involved in or come upon a crash, you must stop, but you should do so in a safe, well-lit public place that does not block traffic if your vehicle can be moved. Then check for injuries, call 911, and exchange information. Stopping in a safe location helps prevent additional collisions.

question: Which best describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They expect no breaks and give none.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They assume other drivers will do the right thing.
note: Defensive drivers constantly consider what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do and stay ready to react safely. They do not assume others will always follow the rules; instead, they anticipate mistakes and leave space and time to respond.

question: When a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane is crossing, must you yield to them?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane have the right-of-way. You must always yield, stop if necessary, and allow them to cross safely. Never honk, rush, or try to go around them.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Squeeze between the large vehicle and the curb to turn,b:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn,c:Turn quickly before the truck or bus finishes its turn
note: Large vehicles need extra space to complete turns; wait until they finish before you turn to avoid collisions.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down help,b:Sound your horn at passing cars,c:Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible
note: On an interstate, only stop for emergencies. Pull completely off the roadway if possible, turn on your hazard flashers so others see you, and stay inside your vehicle with seat belt fastened if it is safe. Walking on the interstate or standing near traffic is very dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful when passing?
options: a:Passing in any marked no-passing zone,b:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing,c:Both of the above
note: Passing is illegal and unsafe in marked no‑passing zones and at or over railroad crossings. These areas have limited visibility or special hazards, so you must stay in your lane and wait until it is legal and safe to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should slow vehicles stay in the left-hand lane except when passing?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Slower traffic should keep right so faster vehicles can pass safely on the left. Use the left lane mainly for passing or preparing for a left turn, not for cruising at a slower speed.

question: Must headlights be on from sunset to sunrise?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Headlights should be on from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is poor, such as in rain, snow, or fog. This makes it easier for you to see and for other drivers to see you, reducing the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when is the correct time to reduce speed?
options: a:As you approach the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.
note: On an interstate, stay at highway speed until you are actually in the deceleration lane. Once in the deceleration lane, reduce speed smoothly to the posted advisory speed for the exit ramp. Slowing too early can surprise drivers behind you and create a hazard in the through-traffic lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly than traffic for 200 feet,b:Wait for a large enough gap to accelerate to traffic speed,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then merge
note: Before leaving the curb, signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder for traffic. Enter only when there is a gap large enough for you to accelerate up to the speed of traffic without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: Does Illinois law require headlights to be on when windshield wipers are in use?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In Illinois, you must turn on your headlights whenever your windshield wipers are in use due to weather conditions. This improves visibility and helps other drivers see you in rain, snow, or other reduced-visibility situations.

question: Under low-visibility conditions caused by fog, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your high beams,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights,c:Increase your speed to clear the area quickly
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights so the light does not reflect back and blind you. If visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe place, turn on your hazard lights, and wait until conditions improve.

question: Is it true that cellphone use while driving is permitted if the driver is over 19 and using hands-free?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In Illinois, drivers may not use a handheld phone while driving, regardless of age. Hands‑free use is only allowed for drivers 19 and older, but even then it is still restricted in certain situations (such as in school or construction zones). So it is not simply permitted if over 19 and using hands‑free" as a blanket rule."

question: What should you do about following distance when driving at night?
options: a:Always use high beams,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights,c:Increase your following distance
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge speed and distance. Increasing your following distance gives you more time to see hazards, react to brake lights ahead, and stop safely if something unexpected happens.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right,b:Passing cars,c:No one
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, including motorcycles and bicycles. You may only complete your left turn when it is safe and there is a sufficient gap in oncoming traffic.

question: Can driving privileges be revoked for giving false information to the Secretary of State?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Providing false information on a driver’s license application is a serious offense. It can lead to criminal penalties and also to suspension or revocation of your driving privileges by the licensing authority.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you,b:Only when slowing down,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot
note: You should check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic behind and beside you. Frequent mirror checks help you spot fast‑approaching vehicles, prepare for lane changes, and react early to changing traffic conditions.

question: As daylight fades, which lighting should you use to help other drivers see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:Parking lights,c:Emergency flashers
note: As daylight fades, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: When driving in fog, should you use high beam headlights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights or fog lights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

question: To restore driving privileges after losing them for failure to pay crash damages, what must a driver do?
options: a:Nothing specific is required,b:File proof of financial responsibility with the Secretary of State,c:Pay a small fine to the court
note: If your license is suspended for failing to pay crash damages, you must file proof of financial responsibility, such as SR‑22 insurance, with the licensing authority before your driving privileges can be restored.

question: Will your driving privileges be suspended if convicted of illegally passing a stopped school bus?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Passing a stopped school bus that is loading or unloading children with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended is a serious offense. A conviction typically results in a mandatory suspension of your driving privileges to protect children’s safety.

question: Is the road surface of a bridge likely to remain icy longer than the rest of the roadway in winter?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze and stay icy longer because cold air circulates above and below them, cooling the surface faster than regular roadways that sit on the ground.

question: If a law enforcement officer stops your vehicle, should you exit immediately and approach the officer’s squad car?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If an officer stops you, stay in your vehicle unless you are told to get out. Keep your hands visible, usually on the steering wheel, and wait for the officer’s instructions. Exiting and walking toward the squad car can be seen as a safety risk and may alarm the officer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you entered an intersection on a green light to make a left turn but the signal then turns red, how should you complete the maneuver?
options: a:Make sure it is clear, then back up from the intersection.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and complete the left turn.,c:Wait in the intersection until the light turns green.
note: If you entered the intersection on green to turn left, you are allowed to clear the intersection even if the light turns red while you are waiting. Move into the intersection, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and when it is safe and traffic allows, complete your left turn to clear the intersection.

question: On a freeway why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards early,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic
note: At freeway speeds, you cover distance much faster, so hazards develop more quickly. Looking farther ahead gives you more time to see slow or stopped traffic, debris, or lane closures and to react smoothly instead of braking or swerving at the last second.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, how should you respond?
options: a:Drive around the gates if you don't see a train,b:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are raised,c:Slow and carefully drive around the gates
note: When gates are down and lights are flashing, you must stop and stay behind the gate line until the lights stop and the gates are fully raised. Trains are often closer and faster than they appear, and going around the gates is both illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Must drivers yield to pedestrians in an unmarked crosswalk?
options: a:True,b:False
note: An unmarked crosswalk exists at most intersections, even without painted lines. Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in or entering these crosswalks on their side of the road when there are no traffic signals controlling the crossing.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, may they use the left lane?
options: a:Yes, they may use the left lane,b:No, they must wait on the side of the road,c:They may cut through all lanes
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and duties as drivers of motor vehicles. When preparing for or making a left turn, a bicyclist may move into and use the left lane or left-turn lane, just as a car would, when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road,b:Switch to high beams,c:Turn your lights on and off repeatedly
note: When oncoming headlights are too bright, avoid looking directly at them. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes, while still checking the road ahead frequently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do regarding oncoming traffic and pedestrians?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians in any crosswalk. Make the turn only when there is a safe gap in traffic and the crosswalk is clear.

question: Should a railroad crossbuck sign be treated like a yield sign?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A railroad crossbuck functions like a yield sign: you must slow, look, and listen for trains, and yield the right-of-way to any approaching train or railroad equipment. Proceed only when you are sure the tracks are clear and it is safe to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it lawful to make a right turn on red after stopping and yielding when not prohibited?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In most U.S. jurisdictions, you may turn right on a red light after coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and all approaching traffic, unless a sign specifically prohibits a right turn on red at that intersection.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic indicates what?
options: a:Passing is permitted when it is safe,b:Both lanes of traffic are going the same direction,c:Passing is not permitted
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line between lanes means traffic is moving in opposite directions and you may pass another vehicle if it is safe and the way is clear of oncoming traffic. Always check for enough space to complete the pass and obey any additional signs or markings.

question: Are taillights required to be illuminated after dark?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Taillights must be on whenever headlights are required, typically from sunset to sunrise or when visibility is poor. They allow drivers behind you to see your vehicle from a distance, reducing the risk of rear-end collisions at night or in low-visibility conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, does the vehicle that arrives first have the right-of-way?
options: a:False,b:True
note: At a four-way stop, the driver who arrives first has the right-of-way and should proceed first after stopping. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. Always move only when it is safe and other drivers are yielding as expected.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you reduce speed below the posted limit?
options: a:Both when driving in unfavorable weather conditions and when approaching/crossing an intersection,b:Only when approaching and crossing an intersection,c:Only when driving in unfavorable weather conditions
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit when conditions are less than ideal, such as in bad weather, heavy traffic, or poor visibility, and when approaching intersections, curves, hills, or narrow roads so you can stop safely if needed.

question: Is it illegal to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving at night with only parking lights is unsafe and illegal. At night or when visibility is poor, you must use your headlights so you can see the road ahead and so other drivers can see you clearly. Parking lights alone are not bright enough for driving.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it required to set the parking brake?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When you make an emergency roadside stop, you should turn on your hazard flashers and, when appropriate, set the parking brake so the vehicle does not roll. However, the law does not always require setting the parking brake in every roadside stop situation; it is a recommended safety practice, especially on grades.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind,b:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost,c:It draws the attention of other drivers
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it can take your hands off the wheel, your eyes off the road, and your mind off driving. This combination of manual, visual, and cognitive distraction greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: What is typically the first skill affected by alcohol use?
options: a:Balance,b:Judgment,c:Vision
note: Alcohol first affects the parts of the brain that control judgment and decision‑making. Even at low levels, your ability to judge speed, distance, and risk is reduced before you notice major changes in balance or vision.

question: If you are turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on your right, should you yield to the bicyclist?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must yield to a bicyclist going straight when you are turning right across their path. Let the bicyclist pass through the intersection or past your turn first so you do not cut them off or cause a collision.

question: Approaching an octagonal traffic sign requires you to:
options: a:Turn.,b:Stop.,c:Slow.
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) red sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Can a parent or guardian cancel a minor's driver license any time before the minor turns 18?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In many states, the parent or legal guardian who signed a minor’s license application can request that the license be canceled at any time before the minor turns 18. This is because the parent or guardian is accepting financial responsibility for the minor’s driving.

question: If weather or darkness reduces visibility, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Speed up to leave the area sooner.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather or darkness, you need more time and space to see hazards and react safely. Increasing your following distance gives you extra room to brake or steer smoothly if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb,b:When pulling next to but not away from the curb,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb
note: You must signal any time you change your vehicle’s position on the road, including when pulling toward a curb to park and when leaving the curb to reenter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your movement and adjust safely.

question: Is it ever safe to stop on railroad tracks even for a short time when moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks. Only enter a crossing when there is enough space for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks on the far side. Stopping on the tracks, even briefly in a line of traffic, is extremely dangerous because a train cannot stop quickly.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, should occupants still use seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Seat belts keep you properly positioned so the airbag can protect you and help prevent you from being thrown from the vehicle in a crash.

question: A traffic sign with an orange background generally indicates what?
options: a:Regulatory requirement,b:Warning in a construction or maintenance area,c:A scenic route ahead
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in construction and maintenance zones. They warn drivers to be prepared for workers, equipment, lane shifts, and reduced speeds, and to proceed with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check blind spots,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane
note: You should never change lanes abruptly or without planning. Safe lane changes require checking mirrors, looking over your shoulder to clear blind spots, signaling in advance, and moving smoothly so other drivers have time to see and react to your movement.

question: Drowsiness, like alcohol or drugs, can do what to your driving?
options: a:Make you a safer driver,b:Improve alertness,c:Impair your judgment
note: Drowsiness slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and impairs your judgment, much like alcohol or drugs. A tired driver may not notice hazards, may react too slowly, or may even fall asleep at the wheel, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: Is alcohol the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Alcohol is a major contributing factor in fatal crashes, but it is not consistently the single greatest common factor nationwide. Other factors such as speeding and failure to wear seat belts also account for a large share of fatalities. The key point for drivers is that any amount of alcohol can seriously increase crash risk and should be avoided when driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds,b:When you cannot see the vehicle over your right shoulder,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
note: After passing on the left, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle (or its headlights at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle. Always signal before returning to the lane and avoid cutting closely in front of other drivers.

question: The three-second rule is useful for determining a safe following distance.
options: a:False,b:True
note: The three‑second rule is a common safety guideline: pick a fixed object ahead, and when the vehicle in front passes it, count “one‑thousand‑one, one‑thousand‑two, one‑thousand‑three.” If you reach the object before three seconds, you are following too closely and should increase your distance, especially in poor conditions.

question: Which actions should you take before changing lanes or attempting to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:All of the above (signal, check mirrors and blind spots).,c:Check your blind spots and mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must signal to let others know your intentions, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Doing all three helps prevent collisions with vehicles you may not see in your mirrors alone.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When another driver makes a mistake,b:Only to help prevent a collision,c:Whenever another vehicle is in your way
note: Use your horn only as a warning to help prevent a collision, such as when another driver may not see you or is about to move into your lane. Do not use the horn to express anger, to punish mistakes, or just because someone is in your way; unnecessary horn use can startle others and is often illegal.

question: How far before meeting another vehicle must you dim your high beams?
options: a:250 feet,b:400 feet,c:500 feet
note: On most U.S. roads, you should dim your high beams at least 500 feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle so you do not blind the other driver. You should also dim your high beams when following another vehicle within about 300 feet so your lights do not reflect harshly in their mirrors.

question: Are drivers required to yield to pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks. An unmarked crosswalk exists at most intersections, even if there are no painted lines. When a pedestrian is in the crosswalk on your half of the road, or close enough to be in danger, you must slow or stop to let them cross safely.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Following a motorcycle too closely is dangerous because motorcycles are lighter and can usually stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you are tailgating and the rider brakes hard or swerves to avoid a hazard, you may not have enough time or space to react, greatly increasing the risk of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to pass on a two-lane two-way roadway within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing?
options: a:False,b:True
note: On typical two‑lane, two‑way roads, passing is prohibited within about 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing because sight distance is limited and cross traffic or trains may appear unexpectedly. You must wait until you are well past these areas and it is clearly safe and legal before attempting to pass.

question: A "No passing zone" sign communicates which message to drivers?
options: a:Increase speed slightly,b:It is not safe to pass,c:Maintain a steady speed
note: A No Passing Zone sign means you must not cross the center line to pass other vehicles in that area. These zones are placed where visibility is limited, curves or hills block your view, or other conditions make passing unsafe. You must stay in your lane until you are beyond the no‑passing area and road markings and signs indicate passing is allowed.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights (regardless of direction or road type)?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights when you are traveling in the same direction, and on most undivided two‑way roads you must stop from both directions. However, on many divided highways or roads with a physical median, vehicles on the opposite side are not required to stop, though they should use caution. Always follow your state’s specific rules, but you are not required to stop in every situation regardless of direction or road type.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, where should you look?
options: a:Look straight ahead.,b:Look toward the right edge of the road.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.
note: When oncoming headlights are too bright at night, shift your gaze slightly to the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare while still letting you track your lane position and see the roadway ahead using your peripheral vision. Avoid looking directly at the oncoming lights, as this can temporarily blind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light when you approach it?
options: a:You are traveling in the wrong direction,b:Treat it like a stop sign and stop before proceeding,c:Wait until it changes to green before moving
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or close to the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when safe,b:Slow and proceed with caution,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light is green
note: At a flashing red light, you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for pedestrians and other traffic, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Which substances can impair driving ability?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter products like some cough syrups and cold medicines. Drugs such as tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives can slow reaction time and affect judgment. Always read labels and warnings and ask a doctor or pharmacist before driving after taking any medication.

question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what is the safest immediate action?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and continue,b:Slow, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway,c:Turn on high beams and proceed with caution
note: When heavy smoke or dust severely limits visibility, you should slow down, move as far to the right as you safely can, and pull completely off the roadway if possible. Stop in a safe place, turn on your hazard lights, and wait until conditions improve so you can see well enough to drive safely.

question: If arrested with a BAC of 0.08% or more, will your driving privileges be suspended for at least six months?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A chemical test showing a BAC of 0.08% or higher results in a six-month suspension of driving privileges.

question: Which situation listed may lead to suspension of driving privileges?
options: a:The individual is over 21 and convicted of illegally transporting alcohol twice within 12 months,b:Three reckless driving offenses in 12 months,c:Drag or street racing
note: Drag or street racing is a serious offense that commonly results in license suspension or revocation in many U.S. states because it greatly increases crash risk and endangers others. Multiple reckless driving convictions can also lead to suspension, but the exact number and time frame vary by state. Transporting alcohol when over 21 is generally not a suspension offense unless it violates specific state laws (for example, open container or transporting for minors). Among the listed choices, drag or street racing is the clearest and most consistently recognized basis for suspension.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance,b:Be ready to use your horn,c:Drive more slowly than usual
note: When following a motorcycle, you should allow a larger following distance than you would for a car—at least three to four seconds. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly, and they are harder to see. Extra space gives you more time to react if the rider slows, swerves to avoid hazards, or loses control.

question: What message appears on a red, octagonal traffic sign?
options: a:One-way,b:Do not enter,c:Stop
note: A red, octagonal (eight-sided) traffic sign always means STOP. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn up the radio to stay awake,b:Increase your speed to finish sooner,c:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap or rest
note: Fatigue impairs driving; stop in a safe location to rest or switch drivers if possible.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving
note: Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for road, traffic, or weather conditions is a major cause of crashes. Higher speeds reduce your time to react and increase stopping distance and crash severity. Safe drivers adjust speed to conditions and stay within legal limits.

question: When there is a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Vehicles in the lane next to the broken line may pass,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side, while a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. When the lines are paired, only drivers on the side with the broken yellow line may cross it to pass; drivers next to the solid yellow line must not pass.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, which of the following should you NOT do?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay off the brakes at first, and let the vehicle slow down gradually while you ease off the accelerator. Once under control and speed is reduced, brake gently and move to a safe place off the road. Hard braking can cause loss of control, especially with a blown tire.

question: Traffic control devices like cones, drums, and signs in a work zone are used to:
options: a:Annoy drivers,b:Inconvenience drivers,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work areas
note: Work-zone cones, drums, and signs are used to guide traffic safely through or around construction areas and to keep vehicles out of hazardous zones where workers, equipment, or road hazards may be present. They protect both drivers and workers by clearly marking where you may and may not drive.

question: If an overhead sign shows an arrow with the word "ONLY" beneath it, what must you do?
options: a:Travel in the direction of the arrow,b:Always make a lane change,c:Look for a destination sign to follow
note: An overhead lane control sign with an arrow and the word "ONLY" means that lane is reserved for traffic going in the direction of the arrow. If you are in that lane, you must follow the arrow’s direction and may not go straight or turn another way.

question: Which driving technique is recommended during inclement weather?
options: a:Steer off the road.,b:Drive in a low gear.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In rain, snow, or other poor conditions, you are more likely to skid if you make sudden moves. Steer and brake smoothly and gradually so your tires maintain traction with the road, and increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react.

question: Is it safe to use cruise control while driving on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You should not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. On slippery surfaces your tires can suddenly lose traction; if cruise control is on, the car may keep trying to maintain speed and can cause skids or loss of control. Always drive manually and be ready to adjust speed smoothly in winter conditions.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee,b:Wait and allow time to pass,c:Take a cold shower
note: Only time removes alcohol from the body; coffee or showers do not speed up alcohol elimination.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, the best course is to:
options: a:Open a window and continue,b:Drink caffeine and keep driving,c:Stop and get rest or change drivers
note: Stopping to rest or changing drivers is the safest response to drowsiness; caffeine or open windows are temporary measures.

question: To obtain court supervision for a traffic violation, must a minor appear in court with a parent and attend traffic safety school?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In many states, including Illinois, a driver under 18 who seeks court supervision for a moving violation must appear in court with a parent or guardian and may be required to complete a traffic safety program. This ensures the minor and parent understand the seriousness of the violation and how to drive more safely.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, how should you act?
options: a:Beep your horn to warn them,b:Expect the child to be fully in control,c:Expect the unexpected
note: When driving near a child on a bicycle, you should expect the unexpected. Children may swerve, stop suddenly, or enter your lane without warning. Slow down, give them extra space, and be ready to brake. Do not rely on your horn or assume the child is fully in control of the bicycle.

question: On an undivided road, when a school bus is loading or unloading children with red lights flashing, must you stop regardless of your direction of travel?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.,c:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
note: On an undivided roadway, drivers in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and is loading or unloading children. You may only proceed once the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to go. The only common exception is when traffic is separated from the bus by a physical median or barrier, as defined by state law.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.,b:If you are under the legal BAC limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
note: Alcohol affects the parts of the brain that control judgment, decision‑making, and reaction time, all of which are critical for safe driving. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair your ability to drive safely, and this can happen even when your blood alcohol concentration is below the legal limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Enter only when there is a safe gap, then accelerate to match the speed of traffic.,b:Use the shoulder to get up to speed.,c:Immediately enter and speed to match traffic.
note: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, you must yield to interstate traffic. Slow or stop if necessary at the end of the ramp, wait for a safe gap, then accelerate firmly as you merge so you reach a speed that fits the flow of traffic. Never use the shoulder to gain speed, and do not force your way into traffic without a safe opening.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow enough to be able to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights,b:Turn on high beams to better see ahead,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible
note: At night on dimly lit streets, you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called not overdriving your headlights. If you go faster than this, you may not have enough time or distance to react to hazards that appear in your lane.

question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, what should you do first?
options: a:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic,b:Press down hard on the accelerator,c:Set the parking brake
note: Before stopping for a signal or sign, check your mirrors so you know where traffic is around you, especially behind you. Then ease off the accelerator and apply the brakes smoothly so drivers behind you have time to react and you can stop in control at the correct position.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, how should you respond?
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,c:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
note: Orange construction signs and cones indicate a work zone. You should slow down, be prepared to stop, and watch for workers, equipment, and lane shifts. Do not assume you can maintain your current speed; adjust your driving to the changing conditions.

question: If you become stranded in a blizzard, should you stay with your vehicle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If you are stranded in a blizzard, it is generally safer to stay with your vehicle. Run the engine only occasionally for heat, keep a window slightly open for ventilation, and make sure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup. Staying with the vehicle makes it easier for rescuers to find you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal for anyone to wear a dual-ear headset while driving?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Driving with both ears covered by a headset or earphones is illegal in many states because it blocks important sounds like sirens, horns, and other traffic. Even where laws differ by state, drivers should keep at least one ear free so they can hear and respond to hazards on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed because you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,c:Merge carefully into the gap when it is safe.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and merge into a safe gap. Do not expect other drivers to give you the right-of-way; you must adjust your speed and position so you can merge smoothly and safely.

question: If a pedestrian is using a guide dog or white cane, what must you do?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,b:You must yield the right-of-way.,c:Honk your horn to alert them.
note: A pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is visually impaired and has the right-of-way. You must stop or yield as needed, give them plenty of space, and never honk or rush them. Allow them to cross safely before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers slow to the posted school zone speed?
options: a:On school days during the posted school zone hours or when school zone lights are flashing, and when children are present,b:Only on weekends,c:Only during recess
note: Slow to the posted school zone speed whenever the school zone signs indicate it and children are present. Many states require you to obey the school‑zone limit during the specific posted hours on school days, or whenever a flashing beacon is operating, even if you do not immediately see children. Always follow the exact instructions on the sign or flashing lights.

question: Do you need to allow as much following distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You should allow at least as much following distance behind a motorcycle as you do behind a car—often more. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver very quickly, and they are harder to see. A minimum three‑ to four‑second following distance gives you time to react if the rider brakes or swerves suddenly.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what is the safest action?
options: a:Challenge them to a race,b:Get out of their way,c:Speed up to avoid them
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, do not respond with gestures, eye contact, or racing. The safest action is to stay calm, safely move out of their way, and let them pass. If necessary, increase your following distance and, when safe, change lanes or turn off the road to avoid further interaction.

question: Is it illegal for drivers under 21 to have any detectable alcohol or drugs in their system while driving?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers under 21 are subject to zero-tolerance laws; any detectable alcohol or controlled substances can result in license suspension and penalties.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams and they blind you, where should you look?
options: a:Look to the left edge of your lane,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane,c:Look straight ahead into the lights
note: When oncoming high beams blind you, do not stare into the lights. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the painted line or road edge as a guide while using your peripheral vision to keep track of the road ahead. This reduces glare and helps you maintain your lane position until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing yellow traffic light, you should:
options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing,b:Stop, then enter the intersection only when it is clear,c:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop unless other traffic, pedestrians, or conditions require you to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Left-turning drivers must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:No one,b:Oncoming vehicles,c:Vehicles overtaking on the right
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are going straight or turning right, as well as to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way unless you have a protected green arrow.

question: If driving in fog, should you use high beam headlights to improve visibility?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights or fog lights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see the road ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it safe to move back into the right lane only when you can see the entire passed vehicle (or its headlights) in your rearview mirror?
options: a:False,b:True
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle (or its headlights at night) in your rearview mirror. This helps ensure you have enough space and do not cut the other driver off.

question: Does talking or texting on a cell phone while driving significantly increase crash risk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving is a major distraction. It takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving and greatly increases your chances of being involved in a crash.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving,b:Whenever you need to use them while moving,c:Before you get into the car
note: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors before you start driving, as part of your pre-drive routine. Set them while the vehicle is stopped so you have a clear view behind and to the sides before you move.

question: Which road surface is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A road in a shaded area,b:A residential road,c:A hilly open road
note: In cold weather, shaded areas freeze first and thaw last because they get little or no sun. Bridges, overpasses, and shaded road sections can stay icy even when other parts of the road look clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but see no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, you should adjust your speed to match traffic and look for a safe gap. If there is no gap, slow down on the ramp so you can merge safely when one appears. Do not force other drivers to brake or swerve, and avoid stopping at the end of the ramp because it makes it hard to accelerate to freeway speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To which pedestrians must you give the right-of-way?
options: a:Only those in marked crosswalks,b:Those in any crosswalk or intersection,c:Only pedestrians crossing at signalized intersections
note: You must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. Even when a crosswalk is not painted, most intersections create an implied crosswalk where pedestrians have the right-of-way.

question: Is it illegal to drink from or possess an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle on a highway?
options: a:True,b:False
note: It is illegal for drivers or passengers to possess an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle while it is in operation.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Continue; you have the right-of-way,b:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing,c:Drive around them by pulling to the right
note: Yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and wait until they have crossed safely before proceeding.

question: Must a motor vehicle's horn be audible from 200 feet away?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Every vehicle must have a horn that can be heard from 200 feet; sirens and bells are reserved for emergency vehicles.

question: Which behavior describes defensive driving?
options: a:Keeping your eyes fixed on the car directly ahead,b:Putting one car length between you and the vehicle ahead,c:Keeping your eyes moving to scan for hazards
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you. By keeping your eyes moving and checking mirrors, you can spot hazards early and have more time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley, building, private road, or driveway in an urban area, must a driver come to a complete stop before entering the roadway?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When you leave an alley, driveway, or private road, you must come to a complete stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway. You must first yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the road, and only enter when it is safe.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly,b:Pump the brakes,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to stop
note: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it down. The system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup, allowing you to steer while braking hard on slippery surfaces.

question: Are most rear-end collisions caused by the vehicle in back following too closely?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Most rear-end collisions happen because the driver behind is following too closely or not leaving enough space to react. Keeping a safe following distance gives you time to brake smoothly if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: When merging onto the freeway, at what speed should you be driving?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway,b:Five to ten mph slower than freeway traffic,c:At the posted speed limit regardless of traffic
note: When using a freeway on-ramp, you should use the acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near the speed of traffic, as long as it is within the speed limit. Matching the flow of traffic makes merging smoother and reduces the risk of sudden braking or collisions.

question: Slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual event on the roadway typically:
options: a:Helps traffic flow,b:Prevents rear-end collisions,c:Causes traffic congestion
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or something unusual, called rubbernecking, disrupts the flow of traffic and can cause sudden slowdowns. This often leads to congestion and increases the risk of rear-end collisions because drivers behind may not expect the slowdown.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you are one vehicle length ahead,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,c:When you are 50 feet ahead
note: After passing another vehicle, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and can return to the lane without cutting them off.

question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic,b:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up,c:Always maintain your position
note: When vehicles are merging into your freeway lane, you should, when safe, adjust your speed or change lanes to create space. Cooperating with merging traffic helps prevent sudden braking and lane changes, improving safety and keeping traffic flowing smoothly.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Wait for the owner to return.,b:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.,c:Call your insurance company when you get home.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a clearly visible note with your name, address, and contact information on the damaged vehicle or property. In many states you are also legally required to report the collision to law enforcement if the damage meets the reporting threshold.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles
note: When you have oncoming traffic on one side and parked vehicles on the other, you should position your vehicle in the safest middle path between them. This gives you maximum space from both potential hazards and reduces the chance of sideswiping a parked car or colliding with oncoming traffic.

question: Signs with an orange background are used for what purpose?
options: a:Construction and maintenance warnings,b:Regulatory messages,c:General warning signs
note: Orange signs are used in work zones to warn drivers about construction and maintenance activities. They alert you to changing road conditions, workers and equipment near the roadway, and the need to slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights,b:Low beam headlights,c:Four-way flashers
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams, and fog lights if your vehicle has them, help you see the road and help other drivers see you.

question: When a train is approaching, vehicles must stop within what distance of the nearest rail?
options: a:Within 15 to 50 feet,b:Within 5 to 10 feet,c:Within 10 feet
note: At railroad crossings where a train is approaching or warning devices are active, you must stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail. This space keeps you safely away from the train and allows room for any overhanging parts of the train to pass.

question: Blue highway signs typically provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services (like rest areas, food, hospitals),b:Construction and maintenance,c:Mileage to destinations
note: Blue highway signs are service signs. They guide drivers to motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals so you can find help and facilities while traveling.

question: May only vehicles displaying special plates or placards for persons with disabilities park in spaces reserved by an official sign?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Parking spaces marked for persons with disabilities are reserved by law. Only vehicles displaying valid disabled license plates or placards may park there, and misuse can result in fines and towing.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, which lights should you use to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Turn on your parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Increase instrument panel lighting.
note: At dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow, visibility is reduced even if it seems light outside. You should turn on your low-beam headlights so other drivers can see you more easily; parking lights alone are not enough.

question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane and skid on water, should the driver immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a vehicle hydroplanes, the tires lose contact with the road and braking can cause a skid. Ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and wait for the tires to regain traction before braking or turning.

question: Is driving allowed while under the influence of any medication that impairs your ability?
options: a:Under no circumstances,b:If it is prescribed by a physician,c:If you do not feel drowsy
note: You must not drive if any drug or medication—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—impairs your ability to drive safely. Even if a doctor prescribed it, you are responsible for not driving while impaired.

question: Are you required to obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:Only during school hours,b:At all times,c:Only if children are visible
note: Drivers must always obey school crossing guards whenever they are on duty, regardless of the time of day or whether children are visible. Their instructions have the same legal force as traffic control devices or police directions and are meant to protect pedestrians in and around school zones.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed,b:Drive at the posted speed,c:Speed up
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and it is easier to lose control. Reducing your speed and driving smoothly gives you more time and space to react and helps prevent skids.

question: What are “No zones” around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into the truck's blind spots or are so close they limit the truck's ability to stop and maneuver,b:Areas with several car lengths between vehicles and the truck,c:Spaces safe to travel behind the truck
note: “No zones” are the danger areas around large trucks where your vehicle may be in the truck’s blind spots or so close that the truck cannot stop or maneuver safely. Staying out of these areas—especially directly behind, alongside the cab, and close in front—reduces the risk of collisions.

question: Orange construction signs indicate what kind of area ahead?
options: a:Roadwork or construction ahead,b:You must change lanes ahead,c:There is a detour ahead
note: Orange signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn of roadwork, construction, or maintenance ahead so you can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Activate your turn signal,b:Reduce your speed,c:Brake hard while in the curve
note: You should slow down before entering a curve so you can steer smoothly and maintain control through the turn. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially at higher speeds or in poor road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears,b:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection,c:Turn left and find another route
note: Even with a green light, you must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. If traffic ahead is stopped and would force you to stop in the intersection, stay behind the stop line until there is enough space to proceed through safely.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Press hard on the brake pedal,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking suddenly,c:Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times
note: If a tire blows out or goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard or sudden braking, which can cause loss of control, especially at higher speeds. Once you have slowed, carefully steer to a safe place off the road.

question: At a railroad crossing, what should drivers be especially alert for?
options: a:Watch for multiple trains.,b:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, hazardous-material trucks).,c:Watch for both multiple trains and vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings.
note: At railroad crossings, you must be especially alert for more than one train coming from either direction or on another track. After one train passes, another may be approaching that you cannot see immediately, so always check carefully for additional trains before crossing.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol level can result in license suspension?
options: a:Any amount,b:0.08 percent or more,c:0.15 percent or more
note: Many states, including Illinois, have zero-tolerance laws for drivers under 21. Any detectable amount of alcohol in the system of an underage driver can lead to penalties such as license suspension, even if the level is below the standard 0.08% limit for adults.

question: Reaction time is slower after which action?
options: a:Drinking alcohol,b:Sleeping,c:Working hard
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain function, reflexes, and coordination. After drinking, it takes longer to notice hazards and react to them, which greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: What do diamond-shaped road signs indicate?
options: a:Warning,b:Stop,c:Yield
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards, changes in road conditions, or special situations such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. They are usually yellow with black symbols, or orange in work zones.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way,b:A slow-moving vehicle,c:Shoulder work ahead
note: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle is the slow-moving vehicle symbol. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or certain maintenance vehicles, so you should be prepared to slow down and pass only when safe and legal.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Maintain a steady speed and allow the pass.,c:Brake hard.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane, maintain a steady speed, and allow the other driver to pass safely. Do not speed up, as that makes passing dangerous, and do not brake suddenly unless needed to avoid a collision.

question: After stopping for a train and it passes, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait for all signal lights to stop flashing and watch for a second train,b:Proceed immediately as soon as the first train passes,c:Ignore signals if you do not see another train
note: After a train passes, stay stopped until all warning lights stop flashing, any gates are fully raised, and you have checked carefully for a second train on any other track. Only proceed when you are sure all tracks are clear and it is safe to cross.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approach, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it passes,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using flashing lights and/or a siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right as you safely can and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, what must you do regardless of your direction of travel?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.,c:Stop, unless your lane is separated from the bus by a physical median or barrier as defined by law.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop whether you are behind it or coming toward it, unless the roadway is divided by a physical median or barrier that separates your lane from the bus. On undivided roads, traffic in both directions must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only when which condition is present?
options: a:Traffic on the street you are turning onto is moving to the left and no sign prohibits the turn,b:You increase your speed before turning,c:Traffic on the street moves to the right
note: You may turn left from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street only if traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left, you are in the proper lane, and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Always yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic that has the right of way.

question: When driving through a work zone, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop,b:Increase your speed to get through quickly,c:Maintain your normal speed
note: When driving through a work zone, you must slow down, obey the posted work‑zone speed limit, and be prepared to stop suddenly. Watch for workers, equipment, lane shifts, and flaggers, and increase your following distance to allow more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder of the road?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must not use the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Passing should be done only in a designated passing lane or where it is legal and safe in the regular travel lane. Driving on the shoulder is unsafe and usually illegal because it is meant for emergencies and stopped vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn must you signal continuously in a business or residential district?
options: a:Not less than 100 feet before turning,b:Not less than 50 feet before turning,c:Not less than 75 feet before turning
note: In business or residential districts, you must signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning so other drivers and pedestrians have time to react. In higher‑speed areas, many states require signaling for at least 200 feet before turning or changing lanes.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend far behind the vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Large trucks and buses have very large blind spots directly behind them that can extend a long distance, often up to about 200 feet. If you follow too closely, the truck driver may not be able to see your vehicle at all. Staying farther back improves your visibility and gives you more time to react if the truck slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing, what should you check?
options: a:Beep your horn,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,c:Flash your headlights
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror and you have enough space to return safely. This ensures you are far enough ahead and reduces the risk of cutting the other driver off or causing a rear-end collision.

question: Must a crash report be filed by the driver regardless of fault if the crash involves death, injury, or property damage over a specified amount?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In many states, you must file a crash report if a collision involves death, injury, or property damage above a set dollar amount, regardless of who is at fault. When any vehicle is uninsured, the reporting threshold is often lower. Always check your state’s specific dollar limits, but remember that serious crashes and those with significant damage must be reported even if you did not cause them.

question: At a red light with a green arrow displayed for your lane, when may you proceed in that arrow's direction?
options: a:When you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear,b:Only after the red light changes,c:Only after coming to a complete stop first
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal for the lane it controls. When you have a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear, after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection. The red light applies to other movements, not to the movement indicated by the green arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates:
options: a:Do not pass,b:Reduce your speed,c:Traffic light ahead
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may not cross it to pass another vehicle. It is used where passing would be unsafe, such as on hills, curves, or areas with limited visibility. You must stay in your lane and only cross the line when allowed for specific reasons, such as turning into a driveway if state law permits.

question: If a pedestrian is using a guide dog or white cane while crossing, must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Pedestrians who are blind or partially blind and using a white cane or guide dog always have the right‑of‑way. You must stop or yield as needed and allow them to completely cross the street before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not working?
options: a:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.,b:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,c:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out, you must treat the intersection like an all‑way stop. Come to a full stop at the limit line or before the crosswalk, then proceed only after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians who arrived first or are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles also turning left,b:All approaching vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard,c:Pedestrians already in or entering the crosswalk
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing your path.
