You do not have to yield to oncoming vehicles that are also turning left into the same street because you will usually turn at the same time into your own lane. The key rule is to wait until all approaching traffic that has the right‑of‑way has cleared before you turn.

question: Make room for cars entering the freeway by:
options: a:Merging into a different lane when possible and adjusting your speed if you cannot change lanes,b:Maintaining exactly the same speed and position regardless of entering traffic,c:Never changing lanes to accommodate entering vehicles
note: On a freeway, help entering vehicles merge safely. If you can do so safely, change to a lane away from the on‑ramp to create space. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed—slightly speed up or slow down—to create a safe gap so the entering driver can merge smoothly.

question: Temporary construction and maintenance signs have which color scheme?
options: a:Orange background with black writing,b:Red background with green writing,c:Yellow background with blue writing
note: Temporary construction and maintenance zones are marked with orange signs with black symbols or lettering. This color scheme alerts drivers to road work ahead and the need to slow down, be alert, and follow any posted instructions.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk,b:You must use due care and yield whenever necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian,c:Only if traffic signals favor the pedestrian
note: You must always exercise due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when they are crossing illegally. However, the law does not give pedestrians the right to step suddenly into the path of a moving vehicle. You are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and whenever necessary to prevent a collision, and you must be prepared to slow or stop if a pedestrian is in danger.

question: At about what speed can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:Around 35 miles per hour,b:Around 45 miles per hour,c:Around 40 miles per hour
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a film of water and lose contact with the road. This can begin around 35 mph on standing water, and the risk increases sharply at higher speeds. Slowing down in wet conditions and having properly inflated tires with good tread greatly reduces the chance of hydroplaning.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your parking lights,b:Use high beams,c:Use low beam headlights
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not bright enough for you to see or for others to see you.

question: If your tires feel like they've lost contact with the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,c:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If you start to hydroplane, gently ease your foot off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake hard or make sudden turns, because that can cause a skid. As your tires slow and water clears, they will regain contact with the road and you can then adjust speed and direction smoothly.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while on the highway helps to:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning,b:Allow you to spot police officers,c:Help you keep up with traffic
note: Looking far ahead on the highway lets you spot slow traffic, hazards, and lane closures early. This gives you time to adjust speed or change lanes smoothly, which reduces sudden braking or swerving and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stop sign that has no marked crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Before entering the intersection,b:At the center of the intersection,c:Only if pedestrians are present
note: At a stop sign with no marked crosswalk or stop line, you must stop before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line or crosswalk, you stop at that line or before the crosswalk so pedestrians and cross traffic are protected.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, what should you try to do with the vehicle?
options: a:Stop in the right travel lane,b:Park with all four wheels off the main-traveled portion of the road if possible,c:Stop where you are and leave hazards on
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, you should, if possible, move it completely off the main-traveled portion of the road. Stopping in a travel lane is extremely dangerous; getting all four wheels off the roadway reduces the risk of being hit by moving traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Enter partially to establish right-of-way,b:Do not enter until you can get completely across,c:Proceed into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through without stopping and blocking cross traffic. Even with a green light, entering when you cannot clear the intersection can be illegal and creates a traffic hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline?
options: a:False,b:True
note: On a two-lane road, a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is not allowed. You may only pass when the broken yellow line is closest to your lane and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Does refusing a chemical test after arrest result in a three-month suspension of driving privileges?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Refusal to submit to chemical testing generally results in a one-year suspension of driving privileges (six months for drivers under 21).

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently,b:Using high beams in fog,c:Staring at the road directly ahead
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the road ahead and behind. Checking your mirrors every few seconds helps you notice vehicles approaching from the rear, lane changes, and potential hazards. In fog, you should always use low beams because high beams reflect off the moisture in the air and reduce your visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed because you have the right-of-way,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians,c:Pedestrians must wait for you to pass
note: A green light means you may go only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk have the right-of-way, and you must wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding, even if your light is green.

question: A large truck turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction may:
options: a:Have to swing wide to complete the right turn,b:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning,c:Complete the turn in either lane
note: Large trucks need more space to turn because their rear wheels track inside the path of the front wheels. When turning right, a truck may need to swing wide to the left before completing the turn. You should never try to squeeze between a turning truck and the curb.

question: The statement 'A teen driver may carry only two passengers under age 20 during their first 12 months of licensing' is:
options: a:True,b:False
note: In many states, including California, a newly licensed teen (under 18) may not transport passengers under 20 years old for the first 12 months unless accompanied by a licensed adult (such as a parent or guardian). Some states allow only one passenger under 20 during this period, with exceptions for immediate family. The statement allowing two passengers under 20 in the first 12 months is more permissive than typical graduated licensing rules and is therefore false.

question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain you should:
options: a:Slow down,b:Drive at speeds appropriate for ideal conditions,c:Apply brakes as soon as your car starts to skid
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to prevent this is to slow down in wet conditions and drive smoothly so your tires can push water away and maintain traction. If you start to skid, ease off the gas and steer gently in the direction you want to go; do not brake hard.

question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way,b:Pull to the left-hand edge of the roadway and stop,c:Pull to the right-hand edge of the roadway and wait for it to pass
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you should safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. This creates a clear path in the center of the roadway so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely. Do not speed up or stop in the middle of the lane.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus on a two-lane roadway with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, must you stop?
options: a:True,b:False
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road from any direction.

question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?
options: a:Stay off the brakes and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go,b:Pump the brakes,c:Apply the brakes lightly
note: If your car begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and stay off the brakes. Braking hard can make the skid worse. Look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, making smooth steering corrections until you regain traction and control.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Be aware of everything happening around your vehicle.
note: To avoid dangerous situations, you must constantly scan all around your vehicle—far ahead, to the sides, and behind. This helps you spot hazards early and gives you time to adjust your speed or position. Simply staring straight ahead or turning off distractions is not enough by itself.

question: Can you use only parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Parking lights alone are not bright enough for driving and are not a legal substitute for headlights at night or when visibility is poor. You must use your headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot clearly see the road or other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross double yellow center lines to pass another vehicle when which condition is met?
options: a:The yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.,b:The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,c:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
note: You may only cross double yellow lines to pass when the line closest to your vehicle is broken and you have enough clear distance to pass safely. A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited, even if the other side has a broken line.

question: After a train clears a crossing with flashing signals, when may drivers proceed?
options: a:As soon as the train passes on the nearest track,b:After the lights stop flashing and you have visually checked for a second train,c:When the gate rises even if lights are still flashing
note: After a train passes, you must wait until the warning lights stop flashing, any gates are fully raised, and you have looked carefully down the tracks for another train before proceeding. Trains can come from either direction and a second train may be approaching on another track.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is actively leading them across the street,b:At all times,c:Only if a crossing guard is present
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and must be given the right-of-way at all times. Slow down or stop as needed and do not honk or try to rush them; allow them to cross safely and completely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian enters after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing and is mid-street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed since you have the green,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane,c:Wait until the pedestrian has cleared the street before moving
note: Yield to any pedestrians already in the intersection; wait until they finish crossing before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another car?
options: a:Under no circumstances,b:If the other vehicle is turning left and passing is allowed on the right without leaving the paved roadway,c:If the shoulder is wide enough
note: You must never leave the paved roadway to pass on the shoulder, but many states allow you to pass on the right within a marked, paved shoulder or right-side area when a vehicle ahead is stopped or slowing to make a left turn and there is enough space to do so safely. You may not use an unpaved shoulder or drive off the main traveled portion of the road to pass.

question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02% has what effect on crash risk?
options: a:It has no effect on driving.,b:It doubles your chances of having an accident.,c:It does not put other drivers at risk.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol in your system can affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Research shows that crash risk begins to rise measurably at about 0.02% BAC, especially for inexperienced drivers. You may feel only slightly affected, but your ability to notice hazards and respond quickly is already reduced, which increases your chances of being involved in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, from which lane should you begin the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb,b:Any lane as long as it's safe,c:The center lane
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start your turn from the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps traffic organized and predictable and reduces the chance of sideswipe or lane-change conflicts during the turn. After completing the turn, you should enter a legal lane on the new street, usually the lane closest to the left curb unless signs or lane markings direct otherwise.

question: If your front right wheel runs off the pavement, how should you re-enter the road?
options: a:Brake hard and steer sharply back onto pavement,b:Ease off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow, then gently steer back on,c:Rapidly accelerate to regain control
note: If a wheel drops off the pavement edge, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Do not brake hard or jerk the wheel. Instead, ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down while keeping the wheels straight. When your speed is under control and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement, then straighten out and adjust your speed to the flow of traffic.

question: If a traffic signal displays a red light and a green arrow, is it true that you may not turn in the arrow's direction until the red light changes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal. It means you may proceed in the direction of the arrow, even if the main red light is on, as long as the intersection is clear and you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection. The red light continues to control traffic going straight or turning in other directions, but it does not prohibit the movement indicated by the green arrow.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid left, how should you steer to correct it?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left toward the skid.,b:Turn the steering wheel to the right away from the skid.,c:Keep your hands off the wheel and do not turn.
note: If the rear of your vehicle starts to skid, you should steer in the same direction that the rear of the vehicle is sliding. For example, if the rear skids left, turn the steering wheel to the left. This helps realign the vehicle with your direction of travel. At the same time, ease off the accelerator and avoid braking hard; if your vehicle has ABS and you must brake, apply firm, steady pressure while continuing to steer in the direction of the skid until you regain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder,b:Attempt to pass or change lanes while in an intersection,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane
note: You should never change lanes or pass while you are in an intersection because traffic can enter from several directions and conditions can change quickly. Safe lane changes require planning: signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and only move when the lane is clear and you are not in an intersection.

question: When a school bus ahead has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.,b:Drive around the bus cautiously.,c:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Children may cross in front of or around the bus, and they can be hard to see, so you only proceed after the signals are off and it is clearly safe.

question: If your license was revoked for DUI, must you meet specific requirements to get it back?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If your license is revoked for DUI, you cannot simply start driving again when time passes. Reinstatement usually requires meeting specific conditions such as alcohol or drug evaluation, completing education or treatment, possible hearings, and paying reinstatement fees. Until you complete the required steps and the state formally reinstates your license, you are not legally allowed to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians even if they walk against the traffic signal?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Pedestrians are required to obey traffic signals, and a pedestrian who walks against the signal generally does not have the legal right‑of‑way. However, drivers still have a duty to exercise due care and must do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even one who is crossing illegally. You should slow down, be prepared to stop, and avoid a collision, but the law does not always give the pedestrian the right‑of‑way when they disobey the signal.

question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of at least what percent?
options: a:0.05 percent,b:0.08 percent,c:0.02 percent
note: For drivers 21 and older in most U.S. states, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. Even at lower levels, alcohol can impair judgment and reaction time, but 0.08% is the common legal threshold for a per se DUI violation.

question: If a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible,c:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, drivers in most situations must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing the road and can be unpredictable around the bus.

question: Which statement is true about large trucks?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly
note: Large trucks are heavier and need more distance and time to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed. Drivers should avoid cutting closely in front of trucks or braking suddenly, because the truck may not be able to stop in time.

question: Which driving abilities are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness,b:Coordination,c:Both alertness and coordination
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow brain function and muscle control, which reduces both alertness and coordination. This makes it harder to notice hazards, react in time, and control the vehicle smoothly and safely.

question: Even a small amount of alcohol in the blood can affect a driver's:
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination,b:Right-of-way privileges,c:Knowledge
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect the parts of the brain that control judgment and physical coordination. This can lead to poor decisions, slower reactions, and difficulty steering, braking, and staying in your lane.

question: When is it necessary to use low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street,b:On a freeway,c:In fog
note: In fog, high beams reflect off the water droplets in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beam headlights aim lower and reduce glare, improving your ability to see the road and be seen by others.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Because they lack adult reflexes,b:Because they are smaller and harder to see,c:Both of the above
note: Children on bicycles are less predictable, may not judge traffic well, and are smaller and harder to see. Because they lack adult reflexes and visibility, you should slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared for sudden moves.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Pull over quickly.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brake and hold it.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and ease off the accelerator. Do not slam on the brakes; brake gently only after the vehicle is under control, then move safely to the side of the road.

question: How does higher vehicle speed affect stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,b:Increase as vehicle speed increases.,c:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.
note: As speed increases, your stopping distance becomes much longer and any crash will be more severe because of higher impact forces. At higher speeds, leave more following distance so you have enough time and space to stop safely.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection instructs drivers to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Stop immediately,c:Stop and proceed only when intersection is clear
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, watching carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians. You do not need to stop unless it is necessary for safety.

question: When passing a line of parked cars, what should you expect?
options: a:That every pedestrian and driver will yield to you,b:That someone or a vehicle may unexpectedly enter your lane,c:That you can drive close to parked cars to make more room for traffic
note: When driving past parked cars, always expect that a door could open or a person, bicycle, or vehicle could suddenly move into your lane. Leave extra space and reduce speed so you can react safely to anything that appears from between the parked vehicles.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road,c:Keep your wheels straight
note: When you park facing downhill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply toward the curb or edge of the road and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn left toward the center of the road,b:Turn right toward the edge of the road,c:Keep the wheels straight
note: On a downhill slope with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway and away from moving traffic.

question: A curb painted red indicates what restriction?
options: a:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,b:No parking, standing, or stopping.,c:Loading zone.
note: A red-painted curb means no stopping, standing, or parking at any time, whether you stay in the vehicle or not, except where signs specifically allow an exception such as for buses.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking your mirrors, what should you do?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots,b:Always slow down in your lane,c:Never look over your right shoulder
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see vehicles in your blind spot that mirrors cannot show.

question: May drivers open car doors on the traffic side only when it can be done safely and without interfering with traffic?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You may only open a door on the traffic side when it is safe and does not interfere with approaching vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians. Always check mirrors and blind spots before opening the door.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates what?
options: a:Stop sign,b:Regulatory sign,c:School zone or school crossing sign
note: A pentagon-shaped sign is used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this five-sided sign, be prepared to slow down, watch for children, and obey any reduced speed limits or crossing guards.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are small and easy to miss, what should drivers do?
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:Make frequent visual checks for smaller vehicles.,c:Always slow down near them.
note: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are smaller and can easily be hidden in blind spots or blend into traffic. Drivers should make frequent, deliberate visual checks—especially before changing lanes or turning—to ensure these smaller vehicles are seen and given enough space.

question: When approaching a construction area, what should motorists do?
options: a:Increase speed to pass quickly,b:Slow down, obey work-zone controls, minimize phone use, and yield as needed,c:Honk repeatedly to alert workers
note: In construction or work zones, you must slow down, obey posted work-zone speed limits, minimize distractions such as handheld phone use where prohibited, and be prepared to yield to workers, flaggers, and authorized vehicles. Driving carefully in these areas protects both workers and drivers.

question: If a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph,b:Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This allows children to get on or off the bus and cross the road safely.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding,c:Yield to pedestrians only
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian already in the intersection. Once the intersection is clear, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Come to a complete stop, check for traffic, and go when safe.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does a "Merging lanes" sign mean drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A merging lanes sign warns that two separate lanes of traffic will soon join. Drivers in both lanes should be ready for vehicles to come together into a single lane, adjust speed, and either merge into the continuing lane or create space so others can merge safely.

question: If you have a tire blowout, should you apply the brakes quickly and then pull off the road?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In a tire blowout, braking hard can cause loss of control. Instead, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, gently ease off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow down gradually, then signal and steer to a safe place off the road before braking lightly if needed.

question: How long must vehicles remain stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing?
options: a:Until all students are off the bus,b:Until the stop arm is retracted and the red lights stop flashing,c:Until the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is fully retracted. The bus does not have to start moving before you may proceed; once the signals are off and the arm is in, you may go if the road is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to make a left turn at a red light from a one-way street onto another one-way street that goes left?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In many U.S. states, you may turn left on a red light from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street where traffic flows to the left, but only after coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic. Always check for signs that prohibit turning on red, because local rules or posted signs can override this general rule.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles,b:You must yield to pedestrians,c:Construction workers must yield to drivers
note: Pedestrians in a crosswalk have the right-of-way and drivers must yield to them unless directed otherwise by a traffic control device.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping
note: At a yield sign you must slow or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard.

question: If you are involved in a minor intersection crash with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave it where it is in the travel lane until police arrive,b:Move the vehicle out of the traffic lane if safely possible,c:Never move the vehicle for any reason
note: If no one is injured and it's safe, move vehicles out of traffic to reduce the risk of additional collisions.

question: Is it legal for a driver to use a hands-free device while driving unless they are under age 19?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In Illinois, drivers age 19 and older may use hands‑free devices while driving, but handheld phone use and texting are prohibited for all drivers. Drivers under age 19 are not allowed to use any cell phone, including hands‑free, except in specific emergencies. Always know your state’s age‑related phone laws and avoid any distraction while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you ever enter an intersection if doing so will leave you blocking it when the light turns red?
options: a:Enter only if you are sure you can clear the intersection without stopping.,b:Do not enter the intersection if you will be unable to clear it completely.,c:Enter only if you entered on a yellow light.
note: You should not enter an intersection unless you are sure you can completely clear it without stopping, regardless of the signal color. Entering when you cannot clear may leave your vehicle blocking cross traffic when the light changes, which is unsafe and can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to drive through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green,b:Follow the officer's directions and proceed without stopping,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions take priority over traffic lights and signs. If an officer tells you to go through a red light, you should follow the officer’s directions and proceed, as they are managing traffic for safety in that situation.

question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You must stay in your lane at all times,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes,c:You may only change lanes from the left lane
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You are allowed to cross a broken white line to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: When following another vehicle at night, should you dim your headlights?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When you are following another vehicle at night, you should use low-beam headlights. High beams can reflect in the mirrors of the vehicle ahead and temporarily blind or distract the driver, reducing safety for both of you.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed,b:Slow down,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, most often at higher speeds. The best way to reduce the risk is to slow down on wet roads and drive smoothly, avoiding sudden acceleration, braking, or sharp steering.

question: How must you yield to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop,b:Stop immediately even if you are in an intersection,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using siren and flashing lights, you must yield by pulling as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is generally:
options: a:Appropriate in all conditions,b:Good if you don’t know the posted speed,c:Often a hazard because it may cause others to pass dangerously
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic, without a good reason, can be dangerous. Other drivers may become impatient, follow too closely, or make risky passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the posted speed or the speed of traffic (up to the limit), adjusting for conditions like weather and visibility.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure about your vehicle position?
options: a:Share the lane with the motorcycle since it is small,b:Blow your horn so the rider moves over,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like a car. When you pass, you must move completely into the passing lane and give the motorcycle full space. Do not share the lane or crowd the rider; treat the motorcycle as you would any other vehicle when changing lanes and passing.

question: How should you behave when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers,b:Decrease following distance,c:Pass carefully, obey all work zone signs, and avoid slowing just to look at the work
note: In construction zones, you must slow down as needed, obey all signs and flaggers, and avoid distractions such as slowing just to look at the work. Maintain a safe following distance—usually more space than normal—because traffic can stop or change suddenly in work areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow centerline means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear,b:Passing is not permitted,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line on your side is broken, you may cross it to pass another vehicle if the lane is clear and you can complete the pass safely before meeting oncoming traffic. If visibility or conditions are poor, you should not pass even if the line is broken.

question: At a school crossing sign (five-sided), what should drivers do?
options: a:Always stop regardless of conditions,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop,c:Always sound the horn when children are present
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. When you see this sign, slow down as needed, watch carefully for children in or near the roadway, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve if there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Only where signs and pavement markings allow passing.,c:Within an intersection if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: Passing is only allowed where signs and pavement markings indicate it is legal and when you have enough clear distance to pass safely. Solid lines, no‑passing zones, hills, and curves usually prohibit passing because you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure the lane is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a steady yellow traffic light and have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Come to a safe stop,b:Speed up to beat the red light,c:Reduce speed and proceed through the intersection
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you are expected to stop if you can do so safely. You should not speed up to beat the red, because the light may change while you are in the intersection and increase the risk of a crash.

question: To reduce the risk of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections,b:Speed up to enter a curve and slow to exit it,c:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill
note: On slippery roads, sudden braking or steering can cause a skid. Slow down before you enter curves and intersections so you can steer smoothly through them without hard braking. Entering too fast and then braking in the curve greatly increases the chance of losing traction.

question: When following a truck at night, should you dim your headlights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When following a truck at night, use low‑beam headlights. High beams reflect off the large side and rear mirrors and can create glare for the truck driver, making it harder for them to see and judge traffic. Dimming your lights helps everyone maintain better visibility and safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Medications for sleep, anxiety, pain, colds, or allergies.
options: a: May impair your driving,b: May increase the bad effects of alcohol on your driving,c: Both of the above
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, including those for sleep, anxiety, pain, colds, or allergies, can make you drowsy, dizzy, or less alert, which impairs driving. When combined with alcohol, these effects can become much stronger and more dangerous, greatly increasing your risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You shouldn’t drive.
options: a: After you have taken any drink drug or medication which changes how you think or act or causes you to be less careful,b: If you are not alert,c: Both of the above
note: You must not drive if you are under the influence of anything that changes how you think, react, or behave, including alcohol, drugs, or certain medications. You also must be fully alert so you can notice hazards and react quickly. If either condition is true—impaired by substances or not alert—you should not drive, so “both of the above” is correct.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: About drugs and driving, what statement is correct?
options: a: Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving,b: Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don’t feel drowsy,c: Only illegal drugs can impair your driving
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can slow your reactions, make you sleepy, or otherwise affect your driving, even if they are legal and properly used. Illegal drugs can also impair driving, but they are not the only concern. Because even non‑prescription drugs can affect your ability to drive safely, the correct statement is that over‑the‑counter drugs can impair your driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a long trip how can you prevent fatigue?
options: a: Get enough sleep before the trip,b: Plan to drive long trips with a companion,c: All of the above
note: To prevent fatigue on a long trip, you should prepare before you drive and manage your trip while you are driving. Getting enough sleep beforehand helps you start the trip rested, and planning to drive with a companion allows you to share driving, stay more alert, and have someone who can notice signs of drowsiness. Using both strategies together is the safest approach, so all of the listed actions help prevent fatigue.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who is most at risk?
options: a: Drivers who are fatigued or drowsy,b: Drivers who are driving on long, monotonous roads,c: All of the above
note: Drivers who are already tired and drivers traveling on long, monotonous roads are both at high risk for drowsy driving. Fatigue slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. Long, boring stretches of road make it easier to lose focus and become sleepy, especially if you were already tired. Because both groups are at increased risk, all of the above is correct.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Fatigue results in an increased risk of:
options: a: Missing an exit.,b: Being late for an appointment.,c: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue and drowsiness make you less alert, slow your reaction time, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. This greatly increases the risk of a serious crash, including running off the road or into other vehicles. While you might also miss an exit or be late, the major safety risk is falling asleep and crashing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you feel fatigued while driving?
options: a: Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.,b: Increase the volume of your radio.,c: Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.
note: Fatigue and drowsiness can affect your vision and increase reaction time to hazards. 'Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.' is the only option that directly addresses the issue of fatigue.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you have an argument with another person and you are angry?
options: a: Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b: Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c: Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions like anger, stress, or frustration can distract you and cause you to take risks or misjudge situations on the road. If you have had an argument and feel angry, it is safer to wait and take a few minutes to calm down before driving so you can focus fully on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Reaction time slows after:
options: a: Drinking alcohol.,b: Sleeping.,c: Working hard.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain function and reaction time, making it harder to respond quickly to hazards. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair your ability to judge distances, react to sudden changes, and control your vehicle safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn quickly, your hands must be:
options: a: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b: Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c: On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: To make quick, controlled turns, your hands should be on opposite sides of the steering wheel, typically around the 9-and-3 or 8-and-4 positions. This gives you maximum leverage and control and allows you to use proper hand‑to‑hand (push‑pull) steering without crossing your arms.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While drinking alcohol, what is a potential effect of taking a prescription drug?
options: a: There will likely be no effect.,b: It will make you more alert.,c: It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription drugs can greatly increase drowsiness, slow your reactions, and affect judgment. Even medications that are safe alone can make you unfit to drive when mixed with alcohol, so you must assume your driving ability can be impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before taking any medicine, you should:
options: a: Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.,b: Have someone follow you home.,c: Keep your window open and drive more slowly.
note: Before taking any medicine and driving, you must know how it will affect you. Read the label and, if you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether it is safe to drive. Many prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can cause drowsiness or other side effects that make driving unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which one of these statements is correct?
options: a: Use your left foot to brake.,b: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c: You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: In normal passenger vehicles with automatic or manual transmissions, you should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent pressing both pedals by mistake and gives you consistent control. The left foot is reserved for the clutch in manual‑transmission vehicles, not for braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these statements about driving while taking medications is true?
options: a: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,b: Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,c: Medications are safe to take at any time
note: Many cold and allergy medications, even when taken as directed, can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time, which can make driving unsafe. You must always check labels and warnings, because both prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can impair your driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should use your turn signals when parking next to a curb
options: a: When pulling next to or away from the curb,b: When pulling next to but not away from the curb,c: Only when pulling away from the curb
note: You must signal any time you change your vehicle’s position in traffic, including when you pull in toward the curb to park and when you pull away from the curb to re-enter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers and cyclists anticipate your movement and adjust safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should use your turn signals in time to let other drivers see your intentions.
options: a: Before you move,b: After you move,c: Only when it’s raining
note: Turn signals must be activated before you start moving, turning, or changing lanes so others have time to see and react to your intentions. Signaling after you move defeats the purpose and increases the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should signal at least 100 feet before turning.
options: a: Before every lane change.,b: At least 5 seconds before you change lanes on a freeway.,c: None of the above.,d: both a and b
note: You should signal well in advance of any change in direction or lane position. That includes signaling before every lane change and for at least five seconds before changing lanes on a freeway, as well as at least 100 feet before turning. This gives other drivers time to see and respond to your actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Use your turn signals.
options: a: When changing lanes or merging into traffic.,b: When turning left or right.,c: Both of the above.,d: None of the above
note: Use your turn signals whenever you intend to change where your vehicle is going in the roadway, including turning left or right and changing lanes or merging. Signaling clearly communicates your intentions and helps prevent crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What happens when you do not signal when required?
options: a: You may get a ticket,b: You may cause an accident,c: All of the above
note: Failing to signal when required can lead to a traffic citation and also increases the chance of a collision because other road users are not warned about your next move. Proper signaling is both a legal requirement and a key safety practice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should bicyclists do to signal a turn?
options: a: Using their vehicle's signal lights,b: Using hand and arm positions,c: Using their horn
note: Bicyclists do not have electric turn signals like cars, so they must use hand and arm signals. To indicate a turn, a bicyclist extends an arm in the direction of the turn so others can clearly see where they intend to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When pulling away from the curb do you need to signal?
options: a: Yes. You need to signal when you pull away from the curb,b: No you only need to signal when you approach the curb,c: only if there are other vehicles around you
note: You must always signal before pulling away from the curb so other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians know you are about to enter the traffic lane. Signaling is required even if you think no one is around, because traffic can appear quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, when is it required to signal?
options: a: At all times,b: Only when there are other vehicles nearby,c: Only when changing lanes on a freeway
note: You are required to signal every time you change lanes, regardless of speed or traffic conditions. Signaling gives other road users time to react and helps prevent collisions, even if you do not see anyone nearby.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to use horn in residential areas?
options: a: Yes, as long as you use it only when necessary for safety,b: It is only legal if you live in the residential area,c: No it is not legal to use the horn in residential areas unless it is an emergency
note: You may legally use your horn in residential areas when it is necessary for safety, such as to avoid a collision or warn others of a hazard. You should not use the horn unnecessarily or just to make noise, but it is allowed whenever it helps prevent danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While making a turn you should signal continuously because
options: a: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b: It lets other drivers know what your intentions are.,c: It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.
note: You must keep your turn signal on throughout the entire turn so other road users clearly understand what you plan to do. Signaling continuously before and during the turn gives drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians time to react and adjust their speed or position, which helps prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To reduce road rage what can you do?
options: a: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b: Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c: Use your horn frequently.
note: Signaling before changing lanes or turning helps other drivers anticipate your movements and reduces surprises that can trigger anger or aggressive driving. Clear, early communication with turn signals is one of the simplest ways to prevent misunderstandings and lower the risk of road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You can use your horn when:
options: a: Another vehicle is in your way.,b: It may help prevent a collision.,c: Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use your horn only when it may help prevent a collision or to alert others to a hazard. The horn is a safety device, not a way to express frustration. Honking just because someone is in your way or makes a mistake can escalate tension and is often unsafe or illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a vehicle is approaching towards you, before how many feet should you switch from high beam to low beam headlights?
options: a: 900 feet.,b: 700 feet.,c: 500 feet.
note: When another vehicle is approaching you at night, you must dim your high beams to low beams within about 500 feet. This prevents you from blinding the oncoming driver, helping them see the road and stay in their lane, which reduces the risk of a head‑on collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver is having trouble seeing other vehicles because of dust or smoke which lights should be used?
options: a: Parking lights.,b: Emergency lights.,c: Headlights.
note: In dust, smoke, or similar low‑visibility conditions, you should turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you more easily. Using headlights (not just parking or emergency lights) improves your visibility to others and helps prevent collisions in poor conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turn on your headlights
options: a: Only when it is completely dark outside.,b: When it is too dark to see from 1000 feet away.,c: When it is too dark to see from 500 feet away.,d: None of the above
note: Headlights are required whenever it is too dark to see people or vehicles clearly from about 1,000 feet away. Turning them on early improves your visibility and makes it easier for others to see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You can drive using only your parking lights:
options: a: 30 minutes after sunset or 30 minutes before sunrise,b: on foggy days,c: Not under any circumstances
note: Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe driving and do not meet legal lighting requirements. You must use your headlights when driving in low‑visibility conditions; parking lights are only for when the vehicle is stopped or parked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving at night on a poorly lit street and using high beams, reduce your lights intensity within 500 feet of:
options: a: a vehicle approaching you from behind,b: an oncoming vehicle,c: a sharp curve or hill
note: High beams can temporarily blind oncoming drivers. You must dim your high beams to low beams within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle so both drivers can see the road safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you be tuning off your turn signals?
options: a: As soon as you have completed the turn or lane change,b: As soon as you begin the turn or lane change,c: Before you begin the turn or lane change
note: Turn signals are used to warn others of your intention to turn or change lanes. Once you have completed the maneuver and no longer need to communicate it, you should turn off your signal so other drivers are not misled.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it necessary to use your headlights while driving on mountain roads and in tunnels?
options: a: Only on cloudy days,b: Only at night,c: Always regardless of weather conditions
note: Headlights should be used on mountain roads and in tunnels even on sunny days so other drivers can see you clearly as light conditions change quickly. This improves visibility for you and makes your vehicle more visible to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signal your intentions with your brake lights or hazard lights when you:
options: a: Need to warn other drivers of an accident or hazard ahead.,b: Are temporarily stopped in a traffic lane for an emergency.,c: Are backing out of a parking space.
note: When you see a collision or hazard ahead, you should warn drivers behind you by lightly tapping your brakes or turning on your hazard lights. This gives following drivers extra time to slow down and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Visibility can be poor during dawn, dusk or in rain or snow. To let other drivers of your presence, you should turn:
options: a: Up the instrument panel lights.,b: On your parking lights.,c: On your headlights.
note: During dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, your visibility and other drivers’ ability to see you are reduced. You should turn on your low‑beam headlights so you can see the road better and so other drivers can see your vehicle from a safe distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Use low beams when approaching another vehicle or when following within 300 feet of a vehicle
options: a: That you are following within about 300 feet.,b: Approaching you from the opposite direction.,c: That is more than 300 feet ahead of you.
note: High beams can blind drivers ahead of you. You must switch to low beams when you are within about 300 feet of a vehicle you are following so you do not shine bright lights into their mirrors and impair their vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When visibility is reduced due to rain, snow, or fog, activate your windshield wipers and use your headlights:
options: a: On the high beam setting.,b: So other drivers can see you.,c: Only when driving on the freeway.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, you must turn on your low‑beam headlights whenever you need to use your windshield wipers. The main purpose is to make your vehicle easier for others to see, not to see farther with high beams, which can reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To be more visible as dusk approaches, you should use your:
options: a: Parking lights.,b: Low beam headlights.,c: Emergency flashers.
note: Use your low beam headlights as dusk approaches so others can see you and you can see the road. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not meant for normal driving visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When following another car after dark, you should:
options: a: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b: Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c: Use your high beam headlights.
note: When following another vehicle at night, keep your headlights on low beam so you do not blind the driver ahead of you. High beams should be dimmed when you are within a few hundred feet of a vehicle you are following.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If visibility is poor due to fog, rain, or snow, utilize:
options: a: Low beams.,b: High beams.,c: Fog lights together with low beams.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can cause glare, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, you may use them together with low beams, but not by themselves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Avoid using your horn.
options: a: When visibility ahead is limited.,b: If you might hit another vehicle.,c: Near blind pedestrians.
note: Use your horn to help avoid collisions, such as when another driver may not see you and a crash is possible. Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians, because they rely on sound cues and may be startled or confused by unnecessary honking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a vehicle's left and right turn signals are flashing at the same time, it indicates...
options: a: It is carrying children to or from school,b: Let the vehicle have the right-of-way,c: There may be a hazard or an accident ahead
note: When both turn signals flash together, they act as hazard lights. This usually means the vehicle is stopped or moving slowly due to a breakdown, hazard, or collision ahead, so you should be prepared to slow down or change lanes safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers are required to, when parking on public roads,...
options: a: Move as far away from traffic as possible,b: Always park on the left side of the roadway,c: Both a and b
note: When you must park or stop on a public road, you should pull as far off the roadway and away from moving traffic as is safely possible. This reduces the chance of being hit by passing vehicles. You do not "always park on the left"; in the U.S. you normally park on the right side, and only where parking is legal and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Feel free to use your horn when driving on tight mountain roads.
options: a: To alert oncoming traffic where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead,b: To let pedestrians know you are there,c: To signal to other drivers that you are in a hurry
note: On narrow or tight mountain roads where you cannot see at least about 200 feet ahead, you should briefly use your horn to alert oncoming traffic to your presence. The horn is for preventing collisions and warning of hazards, not for hurrying other drivers or routinely signaling pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Activate your hazard lights or tap your brake lights if you:
options: a: Need to warn other drivers of a collision ahead.,b: Are temporarily parked in a traffic lane to make delivery.,c: Are backing out of a parking space.
note: If you see a collision or hazard ahead, you should warn drivers behind you by turning on your hazard lights or lightly tapping your brake pedal several times. This gives following drivers extra time to slow down and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you need to park your vehicle outside of designated areas:
options: a: Park with your reverse lights on.,b: Make sure your vehicle is clearly visible to approaching drivers.,c: Park five feet from the curb.
note: If you cannot park in a normal designated area or completely off the road, stop where other drivers can clearly see you and your vehicle from a sufficient distance. Good visibility in all directions gives approaching drivers time to slow down or move over, reducing the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a vehicle malfunction?
options: a: Signal and pull into the slow lane.,b: Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,c: Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
note: If your vehicle has a problem, you should first turn on your hazard (emergency) flashers to warn other drivers. Then, if you can, steer smoothly and safely off the roadway and stop in a safe place away from traffic. Never stop in a traffic lane unless your vehicle is completely disabled and cannot be moved.

question: It is forbidden to drive over a solid double line in the middle of the road to
options: a: Overtake and pass another vehicle,b: Make a left turn,c: Enter a private driveway
note: Double solid yellow center lines mean you may not drive to the left of the lines to pass another vehicle. However, you may usually cross them to make a left turn or to enter or exit a driveway or side road when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited. Passing another moving vehicle over double solid yellow lines is not allowed.

question: You should treat lines as a barrier when:
options: a: Two sets of solid double white lines are spaced 2 feet apart,b: Two sets of solid double yellow lines are spaced 2 or more feet apart,c: Two sets of broken yellow lines are spaced 1 foot apart
note: When you see two sets of solid double yellow lines separated by 2 or more feet, they are treated as a physical barrier. You must not drive on, over, or across them, and you may not use them for left turns or U‑turns except at clearly marked openings. Treat this area as if it were a raised divider.

question: Broken yellow lines are used on streets or highways to:
options: a: Indicate no passing zones.,b: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Broken yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions on two‑way roads. When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass if you can do so safely and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

question: Double solid yellow line markings down the center of a road indicate that passing is:
options: a: Allowed from both directions.,b: Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c: Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mark a barrier between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions. You must not cross them to pass from either direction. You may only cross at permitted openings or to turn where it is specifically allowed by signs or markings.

question: Two sets of solid double yellow lines that are two or more feet apart:
options: a: May be crossed to enter or exit a private driveway.,b: May not be crossed for any reason.,c: Should be treated as a separate traffic lane.
note: Two sets of double solid yellow lines at least two feet apart act as a physical barrier. You must not drive on, over, or across them to turn or make a U‑turn, except at designated openings provided for that purpose.

question: When solid double yellow lines separate the lanes of traffic:
options: a: Passing is permitted from the left.,b: Passing is permitted from the right.,c: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mark a no‑passing zone for traffic in both directions. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle. They act as a barrier between opposing flows of traffic, and you should stay in your lane unless making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road where allowed by local law.

question: You are allowed to pass a vehicle when:
options: a: You are on a hill or curve.,b: You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken yellow center line next to your lane means you may pass another vehicle if it is safe and legal to do so. You must have enough clear distance ahead, no oncoming traffic close by, and no signs or markings prohibiting passing. A solid line next to your lane or limited visibility on hills and curves means you must not pass.

question: What should you do to ensure lane is clear before moving into it?
options: a: Turn your head and look,b: Look in the left side mirror,c: Look into the rear-view mirror
note: Mirrors do not show your blind spots. Before moving into another lane, you must turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This quick head check lets you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be hidden beside you and helps prevent sideswipe collisions.

question: When turning, drivers must signal continuously for the final 100 feet before the turn. How should a driver signal when changing lanes?
options: a: Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder, then change lanes when it is safe.,b: Look over your shoulder then signal and then change lanes.,c: Change lanes and then signal.,d: None of the above
note: When changing lanes, you should signal first to alert other drivers, then check your mirrors, and finally look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. Do not change lanes and then signal, and do not move immediately after signaling without checking traffic. The correct sequence is: signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, then change lanes when it is safe.

question: When operating a vehicle on a road with multiple lanes and traffic traveling in both directions, you must:
options: a: Drive alongside the other vehicles so the drivers can see you.,b: You should drive ahead of or behind the other vehicles.,c: It is safest to drive in the lane next to the center line.
note: On multi‑lane roads with traffic in both directions, it is safer not to drive right alongside other vehicles. Instead, adjust your speed so you are slightly ahead of or behind them. This gives you more space to maneuver, improves your visibility, and reduces the chance of being involved in a side‑by‑side collision.

question: Prior to switching lanes or overtaking another car, it's crucial to:
options: a: Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b: Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c: All of the above.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must both signal your intention and check mirrors and blind spots. Signaling lets other drivers anticipate your move, and checking mirrors and blind spots ensures there is actually space and no one is hidden beside you. Doing all of these steps together is what keeps lane changes safe.

question: Changing from one lane to another is done best:
options: a: Quickly and often.,b: When a car is in your blind spot.,c: Gradually and carefully.
note: Lane changes should be smooth, gradual, and carefully planned. You check traffic, signal, and move over steadily when there is enough space. Sudden or frequent lane changes increase the risk of collisions, especially if another vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Double solid yellow lines indicate that:
options: a: Neither lane may pass.,b: Both lanes may pass.,c: The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions mean that neither direction may pass or cross the lines, except to turn left safely into or out of a driveway or side road where allowed. They act as a strong no‑passing barrier. You must stay in your lane and not drive to the left of these lines unless making a permitted left turn or when directed by traffic control.

question: When driving on a highway alongside a single broken white line:
options: a: You cannot cross the line to pass.,b: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,c: You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe. Always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal before moving across the line.

question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a road with one lane moving in each direction and continually pass the other cars, you will:
options: a: Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b: Increase your chances of an collision.,c: Help prevent traffic congestion.
note: On a two‑lane road with one lane in each direction, driving faster than the flow and constantly passing other vehicles greatly increases your risk of a collision. Frequent lane changes and speed differences reduce your reaction time and surprise other drivers. It is safer to travel at a reasonable, consistent speed with the flow of traffic while obeying the speed limit.

question: What factors make a car accident more likely?
options: a: Looking over your shoulder while making lane changes,b: Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles,c: Adjusting your rearview mirror before you start driving
note: Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles increases the risk of collision. 'Stay in one lane as much as possible. Do not weave in and out of traffic. Last minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.'

question: Which of the following driving behavior below poses a safety risk on the highway?
options: a: Slower traffic must keep to the right.,b: Change lanes without signaling.,c: If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit instead of making a sudden or unsafe maneuver.
note: Failing to signal before changing lanes is dangerous because other drivers, motorcyclists, and bicyclists cannot anticipate your movement. On highways and interstates, you must always signal before changing lanes so traffic around you has time to react. Slower traffic keeping right is a safe and often legally required practice, and if you miss your exit you should continue to the next exit rather than making sudden or unsafe maneuvers.

question: What is true regarding lane changes?
options: a: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.,b: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,c: Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then turn your head to look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. Looking over your right shoulder checks the right-side blind spot for a right lane change; looking over your left shoulder checks the left-side blind spot for a left lane change. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in your blind spots.

question: When operating a vehicle on a road marked with a single, broken white line down the center:
options: a: You must stay within your lane, but you may cross the line to change lanes when it is safe.,b: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,c: You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You must generally stay within your lane, but you are allowed to cross a broken white line when it is safe to change lanes. Always signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before moving into another lane.

question: You are currently in the rightmost lane of a four-lane freeway, and your lane is bordered on the left by thick, broken white lines. This indicates you are driving in:
options: a: The carpool lane and must merge into the next lane.,b: A special lane for slow-moving vehicles.,c: An exit or ending lane that may require you to leave the freeway or merge soon.
note: On many freeways, lanes that are about to end or become exit-only lanes are marked with wide or thick broken white lines on the left side of the lane. If you are in a lane bordered by these large broken white lines, you should be prepared for the lane to exit the freeway or end, and you may need to merge into an adjacent through lane if you do not wish to exit.

question: Diamond-shaped symbols designate carpool lanes. Access to these lanes during the times specified on the signs requires you to...
options: a: Be driving a van or bus,b: Drive at the speed limit or have your lights on,c: Have the minimum number of passengers shown on the signs.
note: Diamond symbols on the pavement mark high-occupancy vehicle (HOV or carpool) lanes. During the posted hours, you may only use these lanes if your vehicle meets the occupancy requirement shown on the signs, such as 2 or 3 people per vehicle, or if you qualify under any listed exceptions. Using the lane without the required number of occupants can result in a citation.

question: You are driving a slow moving vehicle on a winding two-lane highway. You must pull over when it is safe and let other drivers pass when you are followed by
options: a: 3 vehicles,b: 4 vehicles,c: 5 or more vehicles
note: On a two-lane road where passing is unsafe, if you are driving slowly and five or more vehicles are stacked up behind you, you must pull into a turnout or safe area when possible and let them pass. This helps prevent unsafe passing and reduces driver frustration.

question: How do you make a right turn at the next intersection?
options: a: Merge into the bicycle lane before making the turn.,b: Wait until the bicycle lane ends then make the turn.,c: Make the turn from your current lane and do not enter the bicycle lane.
note: To make a right turn where there is a bicycle lane, you should safely merge into the bike lane within about 200 feet of the intersection, after checking mirrors and blind spots and yielding to bicyclists. Then complete your right turn from that position near the right edge of the roadway.

question: When a truck or bus is turning right at the same time you are, you should:
options: a: Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b: Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.,c: Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: Large trucks and buses need extra space to turn right and often swing wide or start from a lane away from the curb. Never try to pass or squeeze between a turning truck/bus and the curb, and do not try to beat them through the turn. Wait until the truck or bus has completed the turn and the path is clear, then make your turn safely.

question: You are getting ready to make a right turn. You should:
options: a: Signal and turn immediately.,b: Stop before entering the right lane and let all other traffic go first.,c: Slow down or stop
note: When preparing for a right turn, you should slow down in advance so you can turn safely and smoothly. Signal about 100 feet before the turn, move close to the right edge or into the right‑turn lane if there is one, check mirrors and your right blind spot, and be prepared to stop at a limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection if required by a stop sign or red light.

question: You want to make a right turn at an upcoming intersection. You should slow down and:
